new_theorems.statement: Inside strict N3(1/128), an exact global physical-star complement relative to one outer hub has automatic two-column diffuse leverage. If C is the full leaf-to-{outer hub, star center} coupling block, then s2(C)>=1-delta with delta=1/128+sqrt(1/128+1/128^2), every row leverage is <0.019293, and the completed two-hub star theorem gives a continuous density with ||p_Q||inf<4.428 and P{Q in I}<4.428|I|.

Inside strict N3(1/128), an exact clique-factor full complement A_ij=lambda v_i v_j whose outer-hub coupling is exactly aligned c=theta v cannot satisfy s3(A)>=1. In both the small-max-coordinate and one-heavy-coordinate cases A is within delta<0.097 in operator norm of an explicit rank-two matrix; in the heavy case rank two follows from det=d_k r^2(alpha lambda-theta^2) at alpha=theta^2/lambda.

designated_partner_applied.actual_inequality: In the exact zero-core global-star subbranch, Delta=det(C^TC)>=(1-delta)^4, hence ||p_Q||inf<=2sqrt(2)Delta^(-1/4)<=2sqrt(2)/(1-delta)<3.131.

next_step: In the exact global clique-factor N3 chamber, elevate the at-most-three rows whose mixed-frame leverage exceeds 1/2 while preserving the third target spectral resource; route the residual to the zero-hubpair, physical-pair, grouped-square, ridge, or mixed-hub endpoints without deleting small nonzero core coefficients.
